decisions.choice: call out to it the proclamation I am speaking to you: Jonah is to say only what God gives him

en.R: This time Jonah obeyed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He got up and went to Nineveh. Nineveh was a very great city. It took a three days' walk to go across it.

ko.R: 이번에는 요나가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀에 순종했다. 그는 일어나 니느웨로 갔다. 니느웨는 아주 큰 성읍이었다. 성읍을 가로질러 가려면 걸어서 사흘 길이었다.

decisions.choice: a great city to God: an exceedingly great city
alternatives: a city great even in God's sight
decisions.reason: Hebrew can use the word for God to make something superlative: "mountains of God" are mighty mountains (Psalm 36:7), and "a great camp, like the camp of God" is a vast one (1 Chronicles 12:23). So "great to God" means very great indeed. The wording may also hint at what the end of the book says outright: the city matters to God (4:11).

decisions.choice: a three days' walk: the size of the city
alternatives: the time needed to cross the city
the time needed to go through all its streets
the size of the whole district around the city
decisions.reason: The phrase gives the city's size in days of walking. Its exact sense is not clear: the time to cross it, to visit all of it, or to cover the whole district of greater Nineveh with its towns (Genesis 10:11-12 lists Nineveh with nearby cities as "the great city"). The walls of Nineveh itself, as later excavated, ran about 7 1/2 miles around. The story's point is that the city was huge, too big to be reached in a day.

decisions.choice: according to the word of the LORD: this time Jonah obeys
decisions.reason: In 1:3 Jonah "arose to flee"; here he "arose and went ... according to the word of the LORD". The repeated "arose" marks the difference.

decisions.choice: a great city to God (L); an exceedingly great city (B); a very great city (R); a three days' walk (all levels)
decisions.reason: As set for Jonah, Literal keeps "a great city to God" and Balanced says "an exceedingly great city" (m1); Readable says "very great". "Three days' walk" stays at every level. Balanced and Readable add "across" to make the phrase read as a measure of size. Readable adds "This time Jonah obeyed" for "according to the word of the LORD", which is what the phrase means after chapter 1 (m3).

decisions.choice: "una ciudad grande para Dios" (L); "una ciudad sumamente grande" (B); "una ciudad enorme" (R); "tres días de camino" at every level
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom, which Balanced and Readable render as a superlative.

decisions.choice: "une ville grande pour Dieu" (L), "une ville extrêmement grande" (B, R); "trois jours de marche" at every level
decisions.reason: As the term sheet; the English meaning decision explains the idiom.

decisions.choice: "mji mkubwa kwa Mungu" (L); "mji mkubwa mno" (B); "mji mkubwa sana" (R); "mwendo wa siku tatu" at every level
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom, Balanced and Readable give its sense, a very great city. "Mwendo wa siku tatu" is the ordinary Swahili measure of a distance by days on foot.

decisions.choice: "하나님께도 큰 성읍" (L); "아주 큰 성읍" (B, R); "걸어서 사흘 길" at every level
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom, which Balanced and Readable render by its sense (meaning decision); the three days' walk stays at every level.

decisions.choice: "một thành lớn đối với Đức Chúa Trời" (L); "một thành vô cùng lớn" (B, R); "ba ngày đường" at every level
alternatives: "một thành lớn trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời"
decisions.reason: As the terms note: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom, Balanced and Readable give its sense, as the meaning decision does; "ba ngày đường" is the ordinary Vietnamese measure of a walk.

records.literal_gloss: And began Jonah to go into the city, a walk of one day, and he called out and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh [will be] overturned.

en.L: And Jonah began to go into the city, a walk of one day, and he called out and said, "Yet forty days, and Nineveh [will be] overturned!"
en.B: Jonah began by going a day's walk into the city, and he called out, "Forty more days, and Nineveh will be overthrown!"
en.R: Jonah went into the city and walked for one whole day, calling out, "In forty days Nineveh will be turned upside down!"

es.L: Y comenzó Jonás a entrar en la ciudad, camino de un día, y proclamó y dijo: «¡Aún cuarenta días, y Nínive [será] trastornada!».
es.B: Jonás comenzó a recorrer la ciudad, un día de camino, y proclamaba: «¡Dentro de cuarenta días, Nínive será derribada!».
es.R: Jonás entró en la ciudad y caminó un día entero, gritando: «¡Dentro de cuarenta días Nínive será destruida por completo!».

fr.L: Et Jonas commença à entrer dans la ville, [la] marche d’un jour, et il cria et dit : « Encore quarante jours, et Ninive [sera] renversée ! »
fr.B: Jonas commença par faire une journée de marche dans la ville, et il proclama : « Encore quarante jours, et Ninive sera détruite ! »
fr.R: Jonas est entré dans la ville et il a marché pendant toute une journée en criant : « Dans quarante jours, Ninive sera détruite de fond en comble ! »

vi.L: Giô-na bắt đầu đi vào thành, một ngày đường, và ông kêu la rằng: "Còn bốn mươi ngày nữa, Ni-ni-ve [sẽ bị] lật đổ!"
vi.B: Giô-na bắt đầu đi vào thành được một ngày đường, và ông lớn tiếng rao: "Bốn mươi ngày nữa, Ni-ni-ve sẽ bị lật đổ!"
vi.R: Giô-na đi vào thành và đi suốt một ngày, vừa đi vừa rao: "Bốn mươi ngày nữa, Ni-ni-ve sẽ bị lật nhào!"

sw.L: Yona akaanza kuingia mjini mwendo wa siku moja, akapaza sauti, akasema, "Bado siku arobaini, na Ninawi [utakuwa] umepinduliwa!"
sw.B: Yona alianza kwa kwenda mwendo wa siku moja ndani ya mji, akapaza sauti, "Siku arobaini bado, na Ninawi utapinduliwa!"
sw.R: Yona aliingia mjini, akatembea siku nzima, akitangaza, "Baada ya siku arobaini Ninawi utapinduliwa juu chini!"

ko.L: 그리고 요나가 그 성읍에 들어가기 시작하여 하룻길을 [걸어가며] 외쳐 말했다. "사십 일이 더 지나면, 니느웨가 뒤엎어질 것이다!"
ko.B: 요나는 그 성읍으로 들어가 하룻길을 걸으며 외쳤다. "사십 일이 지나면 니느웨가 뒤엎어진다!"
ko.R: 요나는 성읍에 들어가 꼬박 하루 동안 걸으면서 외쳤다. "사십 일 뒤에 니느웨는 완전히 뒤집힐 것이다!"

decisions.choice: overturned: destroyed, as Sodom was; and also, unknowingly, turned around
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19:21, 25, 29; Deuteronomy 29:22). Jonah means destruction. But the same verb means to turn or change (Exodus 7:17; 1 Samuel 10:9; Psalm 30:12), and in forty days Nineveh is indeed turned: from its evil ways (verse 10). The word holds both outcomes.

decisions.choice: Jonah's message: five words, with no call to repent and no name of God
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the message is only five words: "Yet forty days, and Nineveh overturned." It does not say who will do it or why, and offers no way out. The people of Nineveh respond anyway (verse 5).

decisions.choice: forty days: a set time of testing and waiting
decisions.reason: Forty days is a common period in the Bible: the flood rains (Genesis 7:4), Moses on the mountain (Exodus 24:18), Elijah's journey to Horeb (1 Kings 19:8). It gave the city time.

decisions.choice: a walk of one day: on the first day of his walk through the city
decisions.reason: Jonah had gone one day's walk into the city of verse 3's three days when he began to call out. The text does not say whether he kept on after that.

decisions.choice: overturned (L); overthrown (B); turned upside down (R)
decisions.reason: Each level chooses an English verb that can carry both senses of the Hebrew (m1): ruin, and a complete change. Readable's "turned upside down" does so in everyday words.

decisions.choice: "trastornada" (L); "derribada" (B); "destruida por completo" (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "trastornar" means both to overturn and to turn around, so Literal keeps something of the double sense the meaning decision describes; Balanced and Readable give the threatened destruction.

decisions.choice: "renversée" (L), "détruite" (B), "détruite de fond en comble" (R)
decisions.reason: The English meaning decision gives the double sense (destroyed, and turned around); Literal keeps the image of overturning, Balanced and Readable the threatened sense, which is what Jonah means.

decisions.choice: "kupindua" (overturn) at every level
decisions.reason: Swahili "kupindua" is used of overthrowing a city or a ruler and of turning a thing over, so it keeps both senses the meaning decision names: destruction, as Sodom, and an unknowing hint that the city will be turned around. Readable adds "juu chini", upside down, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "뒤엎어지다" (L, B); "완전히 뒤집히다" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for Sodom (meaning decision; Gen 19:25 "뒤엎으셨다"), and it can also mean "turned around". Korean "뒤엎다, 뒤집다" keeps the overthrow and leaves the second sense open, as the footnote explains.

decisions.choice: "lật đổ" (L, B); "lật nhào" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning footnote says the word means destroyed, as Sodom was, and also, unknowingly, turned around; "lật" keeps the picture of overturning that carries both senses, where "hủy diệt" would keep only one.

source.text: וַֽיַּאֲמִ֛ינוּ אַנְשֵׁ֥י נִֽינְוֵ֖ה בֵּֽאלֹהִ֑ים וַיִּקְרְאוּ־צוֹם֙ וַיִּלְבְּשׁ֣וּ שַׂקִּ֔ים מִגְּדוֹלָ֖ם וְעַד־קְטַנָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And believed [the] men of Nineveh in God, and they proclaimed a fast, and they put on sackcloth, from their great to their small.

en.L: And {{gender:the people|the men}} of Nineveh believed in God, and they called a fast and clothed themselves [in] sackcloth, from their greatest even to their least.
en.B: The people of Nineveh believed God. They called for a fast and dressed in sackcloth, from the greatest to the least of them.
en.R: The people of Nineveh believed God's message. They decided to go without food, and they all put on rough sackcloth. Everyone did this, from the most important people to the least important.

es.L: Y {{gender:los habitantes|los hombres}} de Nínive creyeron en Dios, y proclamaron ayuno y se vistieron de cilicio, desde el mayor de ellos hasta el menor.
es.B: La gente de Nínive creyó a Dios. Proclamaron un ayuno y se vistieron de cilicio, desde el mayor hasta el menor de ellos.
es.R: La gente de Nínive creyó el mensaje de Dios. Decidieron dejar de comer, y todos se pusieron ropa áspera de luto. Todos lo hicieron, desde los más importantes hasta los menos importantes.

fr.L: Et {{gender:les gens|les hommes}} de Ninive crurent en Dieu, et ils proclamèrent un jeûne et se revêtirent de sacs, depuis le plus grand d’entre eux jusqu’au plus petit.
fr.B: Les habitants de Ninive crurent en Dieu. Ils proclamèrent un jeûne et se vêtirent de sacs, du plus grand jusqu’au plus petit.
fr.R: Les habitants de Ninive ont cru au message de Dieu. Ils ont décidé de ne plus manger, et ils ont tous mis des vêtements de toile de sac. Tout le monde l’a fait, des gens les plus importants jusqu’aux moins importants.

vi.L: Dân thành Ni-ni-ve tin Đức Chúa Trời, và họ rao truyền một kỳ kiêng ăn và mặc vải thô, từ người lớn nhất cho đến người nhỏ nhất trong họ.
vi.B: Dân thành Ni-ni-ve tin Đức Chúa Trời. Họ công bố một kỳ kiêng ăn và mặc vải thô, từ người lớn nhất đến người nhỏ nhất.
vi.R: Dân thành Ni-ni-ve tin sứ điệp của Đức Chúa Trời. Họ quyết định nhịn ăn, và ai nấy đều mặc vải thô. Mọi người đều làm như vậy, từ người quyền thế nhất đến người thấp kém nhất.

sw.L: Na watu wa Ninawi wakamwamini Mungu, wakatangaza mfungo, wakavaa nguo za magunia, tangu mkubwa wao hata mdogo wao.
sw.B: Watu wa Ninawi walimwamini Mungu. Wakatangaza mfungo, wakavaa nguo za magunia, tangu mkubwa hadi mdogo kati yao.
sw.R: Watu wa Ninawi waliuamini ujumbe wa Mungu. Waliamua kufunga, wasile chakula, na wote wakavaa nguo mbaya za magunia. Kila mtu alifanya hivyo, tangu wakubwa mpaka wadogo.

ko.L: 그리고 니느웨 사람들이 하나님을 믿고, 금식을 선포하고, 가장 큰 자부터 가장 작은 자까지 굵은 베옷을 입었다.
ko.B: 니느웨 사람들은 하나님을 믿었다. 그들은 금식을 선포하고, 높은 사람부터 낮은 사람까지 모두 굵은 베옷을 입었다.
ko.R: 니느웨 사람들은 하나님의 말씀을 믿었다. 그들은 음식을 먹지 않기로 하고, 모두 거친 베옷을 입었다. 높은 사람부터 낮은 사람까지 모두 그렇게 했다.

decisions.choice: the people of Nineveh believed God: they took his warning as true and acted on it
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of Abraham, who "believed the LORD" (Genesis 15:6). The people trust that the warning comes from God and turn to him. The narrator calls him "God" throughout the story of Nineveh, not by the name the LORD, which Israel knew.

decisions.choice: a fast and sackcloth: signs of grief and repentance
decisions.reason: To go without food and to wear sackcloth, a coarse cloth of goat or camel hair, were signs of mourning and of humbling oneself before God (1 Kings 21:27; Joel 1:13-14). The whole city, high and low, took part.

decisions.choice: Nineveh repented at Jonah's preaching: as Matthew 12:41
decisions.reason: Jesus says that the people of Nineveh will rise at the judgment and condemn his generation, "because they repented at the preaching of Jonah" (Matthew 12:41; Luke 11:32).

decisions.choice: believed in God (L); believed God (B); believed God's message (R); go without food (R); rough sackcloth (R)
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that the people believed what God said through Jonah, explains a fast as going without food, and adds "rough" to show what sackcloth was. "The men of Nineveh" means all its people, so Literal has a gender setting, as Matthew 12:41 does.

decisions.choice: "cilicio" (L, B); "ropa áspera de luto" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled Spanish for sackcloth in the prophets. "Los habitantes" follows Matthew 12:41 L, with "los hombres" as the gender alternative.

decisions.choice: "les gens" with "les hommes" as the gender alternative (L); "Les habitants de Ninive" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English Literal; Balanced and Readable say "habitants", which already includes everyone.

decisions.choice: "watu" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Swahili "watu" (people) already includes men and women, and the only other word, "wanaume" (males), would change the meaning; so where the English has a gender span (here, and "mwanadamu" in 3:7-8, "yake" in 3:8), the Swahili has none. Noted once for these books.

decisions.choice: "니느웨 사람들" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean "사람들" already includes men and women (style guide section 7), so the English gender span at Literal has nothing to change; the same holds for "사람과 짐승" in 3:7-8 and "자기의" in 3:8. Matthew 12:41 also says "니느웨 사람들".

decisions.choice: "굵은 베옷" (L, B); "거친 베옷" (R); "금식을 선포하다" (L, B); "음식을 먹지 않기로 하다" (R)
decisions.reason: Sackcloth and fasting are signs of grief and repentance (meaning decision); Readable says plainly what a fast is, as the English Readable.

decisions.choice: "Dân thành Ni-ni-ve" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "the men" as a gender alternative; Vietnamese "dân thành" already covers the whole population and has no second wording to offer, so there is no span, as the style guide asks. Sackcloth is "vải thô", as the Isaiah and Jeremiah note.

source.text: וַיִּגַּ֤ע הַדָּבָר֙ אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךנִֽינְוֵ֔ה וַיָּ֨קָם֙ מִכִּסְא֔וֹ וַיַּעֲבֵ֥ר אַדַּרְתּ֖וֹ מֵֽעָלָ֑יו וַיְכַ֣ס שַׂ֔ק וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב עַל־הָאֵֽפֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And reached the word to [the] king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne and took off his robe from on him, and covered [himself with] sackcloth, and sat on the ashes.

en.L: And the word reached the king of Nineveh, and he rose up from his throne, and removed his robe from himself, and covered himself [with] sackcloth, and sat on the ashes.
en.B: When the news reached the king of Nineveh, he rose from his throne, laid aside his royal robe, covered himself with sackcloth and sat down in the ashes.
en.R: When the king of Nineveh heard about this, he got up from his throne. He took off his royal robes and put on sackcloth. Then he sat down in the ashes.

es.L: Y llegó la palabra al rey de Nínive, y se levantó de su trono, y se quitó de encima su manto, y se cubrió [de] cilicio, y se sentó sobre la ceniza.
es.B: Cuando la noticia llegó al rey de Nínive, este se levantó de su trono, se quitó su manto real, se cubrió de cilicio y se sentó en la ceniza.
es.R: Cuando el rey de Nínive se enteró de esto, se levantó de su trono. Se quitó sus ropas reales y se puso ropa áspera de luto. Luego se sentó en la ceniza.

fr.L: Et la parole parvint au roi de Ninive, et il se leva de son trône, et ôta son manteau de dessus lui, et se couvrit d’un sac, et s’assit sur la cendre.
fr.B: Quand la nouvelle parvint au roi de Ninive, il se leva de son trône, quitta son manteau royal, se couvrit d’un sac et s’assit dans la cendre.
fr.R: Quand le roi de Ninive a appris la nouvelle, il s’est levé de son trône. Il a enlevé ses vêtements royaux et il a mis un vêtement de toile de sac. Puis il s’est assis dans la cendre.

vi.L: Lời ấy đến tai vua Ni-ni-ve, và vua đứng dậy khỏi ngai mình, cởi áo choàng khỏi mình, quấn mình [bằng] vải thô, và ngồi trên tro.
vi.B: Khi tin ấy đến tai vua Ni-ni-ve, vua đứng dậy khỏi ngai, cởi bỏ áo bào, quấn vải thô và ngồi trong đống tro.
vi.R: Khi vua Ni-ni-ve nghe tin này, vua đứng dậy khỏi ngai. Vua cởi áo bào ra và mặc vải thô. Rồi vua ngồi xuống trong đống tro.

sw.L: Neno hilo likamfikia mfalme wa Ninawi, naye akainuka kutoka kiti chake cha enzi, akavua joho lake, akajifunika nguo ya magunia, akaketi juu ya majivu.
sw.B: Habari hizo zilipomfikia mfalme wa Ninawi, aliinuka kutoka kiti chake cha enzi, akavua vazi lake la kifalme, akajifunika nguo ya magunia, akaketi katika majivu.
sw.R: Mfalme wa Ninawi aliposikia habari hizo, aliinuka kutoka kiti chake cha enzi. Akavua mavazi yake ya kifalme, akavaa nguo ya magunia. Kisha akaketi chini katika majivu.

ko.L: 그리고 그 말이 니느웨 왕에게 이르니, 그가 자기 보좌에서 일어나 자기 몸에서 겉옷을 벗고, 굵은 베옷을 덮어쓰고 잿더미 위에 앉았다.
ko.B: 이 소식이 니느웨 왕에게 전해지자, 왕은 보좌에서 일어나 왕의 겉옷을 벗고, 굵은 베옷을 걸치고 잿더미에 앉았다.
ko.R: 니느웨 왕도 이 소식을 들었다. 그는 왕좌에서 일어나 왕의 옷을 벗고 베옷을 입었다. 그리고 잿더미에 주저앉았다.

decisions.choice: the word: the news of Jonah's message and of the people's response
decisions.reason: The word can mean Jonah's proclamation or the report of what was happening in the city. Either way, the king hears it after the people have already begun to fast; the movement starts among the people and reaches the throne.

decisions.choice: the king of Nineveh: the king is not named
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in the Bible the Assyrian ruler is called "the king of Assyria". This book names him by his city, as it is the city that matters in the story, and gives no name or date.

decisions.choice: rose from his throne, took off his robe, sat in the ashes: the king humbles himself
decisions.reason: Each act reverses his royal state: from the throne to the ashes, from the royal robe to sackcloth. Sitting in ashes or dust was a sign of deep grief and repentance (Job 2:8; 42:6; Isaiah 58:5).

decisions.choice: royal robe (B); royal robes (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means a fine cloak, here the king's. Balanced and Readable add "royal" to make that plain.

source.text: וַיַּזְעֵ֗ק וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ בְּנִֽינְוֵ֔ה מִטַּ֧עַם הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וּגְדֹלָ֖יו לֵאמֹ֑ר הָאָדָ֨ם וְהַבְּהֵמָ֜ה הַבָּקָ֣ר וְהַצֹּ֗אן אַֽל־יִטְעֲמוּ֙ מְא֔וּמָה אַ֨ל־יִרְע֔וּ וּמַ֖יִם אַל־יִשְׁתּֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he had it proclaimed and said in Nineveh, by decree of the king and his great ones, saying: The man and the beast, the herd and the flock, let them not taste anything; let them not graze, and water let them not drink.

en.L: And he had [it] proclaimed, and he said in Nineveh, by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying: "{{gender:Humans|Man}} and beast, herd and flock, let them not taste anything; let them not graze, and let them not drink water.
en.B: Then he had a proclamation made in Nineveh: "By order of the king and his nobles: Let no person or animal, herd or flock, taste anything at all. They must not graze, and they must not drink water.
en.R: Then he sent out this order to everyone in Nineveh: "This is a command from the king and his nobles: No person or animal may eat anything. Do not let the cattle, sheep or goats graze. Nobody, not even the animals, may drink any water.

es.L: E hizo proclamar y dijo en Nínive, por decreto del rey y de sus nobles, diciendo: «{{gender:Personas|Hombres}} y bestias, ganado y rebaño, que no prueben nada; que no pasten, y que no beban agua.
es.B: Luego hizo pregonar en Nínive: «Por orden del rey y de sus nobles: Que ninguna persona ni animal, ni ganado ni rebaño, pruebe bocado. Que no pasten ni beban agua.
es.R: Luego mandó anunciar esta orden a todos en Nínive: «Este es un mandato del rey y de sus nobles: Ninguna persona ni animal puede comer nada. Que no pasten las vacas, las ovejas ni las cabras. Nadie, ni siquiera los animales, puede beber agua.

fr.L: Et il fit crier, et il dit dans Ninive, par décret du roi et de ses grands, disant : « Que {{gender:les humains|les hommes}} et les bêtes, le gros et le petit bétail, ne goûtent à rien ; qu’ils ne paissent pas, et qu’ils ne boivent pas d’eau.
fr.B: Puis il fit proclamer dans Ninive : « Par ordre du roi et de ses grands : que ni être humain ni bête, ni gros ni petit bétail, ne goûte à quoi que ce soit. Qu’ils ne mangent pas et ne boivent pas d’eau.
fr.R: Puis il a envoyé cet ordre à tous les habitants de Ninive : « Voici ce que commandent le roi et ses grands : Personne ne doit rien manger, ni les gens ni les animaux. Ne laissez pas les bœufs, les moutons et les chèvres aller brouter. Personne, pas même les animaux, ne doit boire d’eau.

vi.L: Vua cho rao báo và nói trong Ni-ni-ve, theo sắc lệnh của vua và các quan đại thần, rằng: "Người và thú vật, bò và chiên, không được nếm gì cả; không được ăn cỏ, và không được uống nước.
vi.B: Rồi vua cho truyền rao khắp Ni-ni-ve: "Theo lệnh của vua và các quan đại thần: Người và thú vật, bò và chiên, đều không được nếm bất cứ thứ gì. Chúng không được ăn cỏ, cũng không được uống nước.
vi.R: Rồi vua ra lệnh cho mọi người trong thành Ni-ni-ve: "Đây là lệnh của vua và các quan đại thần: Không người nào hay con vật nào được ăn gì cả. Không được cho bò, chiên hay dê ra đồng ăn cỏ. Không ai, kể cả thú vật, được uống nước.

sw.L: Kisha akatangaza [habari], akasema katika Ninawi, kwa amri ya mfalme na wakuu wake, kusema: "Mwanadamu wala mnyama, ng'ombe wala kondoo, wasionje kitu chochote; wasile malisho, wala wasinywe maji.
sw.B: Kisha akapiga mbiu katika Ninawi: "Kwa amri ya mfalme na wakuu wake: Mtu yeyote au mnyama, ng'ombe au kondoo, asionje kitu chochote. Wasile malisho, wala wasinywe maji.
sw.R: Kisha akatuma amri hii kwa kila mtu katika Ninawi: "Hii ni amri ya mfalme na wakuu wake: Mtu yeyote wala mnyama asile chochote. Msiwaache ng'ombe, kondoo wala mbuzi wale majani. Mtu yeyote asinywe maji, wala wanyama wasinywe.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 니느웨에 선포하게 하여 말했다. 왕과 그의 대신들의 명령으로 이르기를, "사람과 짐승, 소 떼와 양 떼는 아무것도 맛보지 말고, 풀을 뜯지도 말고, 물을 마시지도 말아라.
ko.B: 그리고 왕은 니느웨에 이렇게 선포하게 했다. "왕과 대신들의 명령이다. 사람이든 짐승이든, 소 떼든 양 떼든 아무것도 먹지 말아라. 풀을 뜯어서도 안 되고, 물을 마셔서도 안 된다.
ko.R: 그리고 왕은 니느웨의 모든 사람에게 이렇게 명령을 내렸다. "왕과 대신들이 내리는 명령이다. 사람도 짐승도 아무것도 먹지 말아라. 소나 양이나 염소에게도 풀을 뜯기지 말아라. 아무도, 짐승까지도 물을 마시지 말아라.

decisions.choice: the decree of the king and his nobles: an official proclamation
decisions.reason: The word for decree is a term for the order of a ruler, used of royal commands in Ezra and Daniel. The king acts with his nobles, his great men, so that the order carries the full weight of the state.

decisions.choice: people and animals: the whole city, its animals included, is to fast
decisions.reason: Including the animals makes the fast total: no living thing in the city is to eat or drink. The animals also share in the sackcloth (verse 8). God's last words in the book mention the animals of Nineveh (4:11).

decisions.choice: Humans and beast (L); person or animal (B, R); cattle, sheep or goats (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for human beings is inclusive here, set against the animals; Literal gives it a gender setting, and Balanced and Readable say "person". Readable spells out "herd and flock" as cattle, sheep and goats, and makes clear that the animals too are not to drink. The decree runs to the end of verse 9.

decisions.choice: jussive subjunctives: "que no prueben nada" (L); "Que ninguna persona ... pruebe bocado" (B)
decisions.reason: The decree is worded with Spanish jussive subjunctives, as the term sheet sets for 3:7-8.

decisions.choice: "les humains" with "les hommes" as the gender alternative (L); "être humain" (B), "les gens" (R) without a setting; the decree's « » stays open to the end of 3:9
alternatives: "les hommes et les bêtes" with no setting
decisions.reason: The English Literal has a gender span on "Humans"; Balanced and Readable already say it inclusively. The king's decree runs over three verses, so its quotation marks close only at its end.

decisions.choice: "akapiga mbiu"
decisions.reason: The Swahili phrase for a public proclamation cried through a town, which is what the king's decree was.

decisions.choice: The king's decree in 해라체; "대신들" for his nobles
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: the king of Nineveh's decree is 해라체, as Persian decrees in Ezra. "대신" is the word for a king's high officials [Dan 6:3].

decisions.choice: the king is "vua" in the narration and the decree speaks impersonally
decisions.reason: The terms note: the king of Nineveh's decree is impersonal ("người và súc vật ..."), with "ta" only where the king speaks in his own person, which he does not here. "Người" covers men and women, so the English gender span has no Vietnamese counterpart.

source.text: וְיִתְכַּסּ֣וּ שַׂקִּ֗ים הָֽאָדָם֙ וְהַבְּהֵמָ֔ה וְיִקְרְא֥וּ אֶל־אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּחָזְקָ֑ה וְיָשֻׁ֗בוּ אִ֚ישׁ מִדַּרְכּ֣וֹ הָֽרָעָ֔ה וּמִן־הֶחָמָ֖ס אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּכַפֵּיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And let them cover themselves [with] sackcloth, the man and the beast, and let them call to God with strength, and let them turn, each from his evil way and from the violence that [is] in their palms.

en.L: And let them cover themselves [with] sackcloth, {{gender:humans|man}} and beast, and let them call to God with strength, and let them turn, each from {{gender:their|his}} evil way and from the violence that [is] in their palms.
en.B: People and animals alike must be covered with sackcloth. Let them call out to God with all their might, and let each one turn from {{gender:their|his}} evil ways and from the violence they do.
en.R: Everyone, people and animals, must wear sackcloth. Everyone must pray to God with all their strength. They must all stop doing evil things and stop hurting others.

es.L: Y que se cubran [de] cilicio {{gender:personas|hombres}} y bestias, y que clamen a Dios con fuerza, y que se vuelvan cada uno de su mal camino y de la violencia que [hay] en las palmas de sus manos.
es.B: Personas y animales por igual deben cubrirse de cilicio. Que clamen a Dios con todas sus fuerzas, y que cada uno se vuelva de su mal camino y de la violencia que comete.
es.R: Todos, personas y animales, deben vestirse con ropa áspera de luto. Todos deben orar a Dios con todas sus fuerzas. Todos deben dejar de hacer el mal y de hacer daño a los demás.

fr.L: Et qu’ils se couvrent de sacs, {{gender:les humains|les hommes}} et les bêtes, et qu’ils crient vers Dieu avec force, et qu’ils reviennent, chacun de sa voie mauvaise et de la violence qui [est] dans leurs paumes.
fr.B: Que les êtres humains et les animaux soient couverts de sacs. Qu’ils crient vers Dieu de toutes leurs forces, et que chacun revienne de sa mauvaise conduite et de la violence qu’il commet.
fr.R: Tout le monde, les gens et les animaux, doit porter un vêtement de toile de sac. Tout le monde doit prier Dieu de toutes ses forces. Il faut que chacun arrête de faire le mal et de faire du tort aux autres.

vi.L: Người và thú vật hãy quấn mình [bằng] vải thô, và hãy hết sức kêu cầu Đức Chúa Trời, và mỗi người hãy quay lại khỏi đường ác của mình và khỏi sự bạo ngược trong lòng bàn tay của họ.
vi.B: Người và thú vật đều phải quấn vải thô. Mọi người hãy hết sức kêu cầu Đức Chúa Trời, và mỗi người phải từ bỏ đường lối gian ác của mình và những việc hung bạo mình đã làm.
vi.R: Mọi người và mọi con vật đều phải mặc vải thô. Ai nấy phải hết sức cầu nguyện với Đức Chúa Trời. Mọi người phải thôi làm điều ác và thôi làm hại người khác.

sw.L: Na wajifunike nguo za magunia, mwanadamu na mnyama, na wamlilie Mungu kwa nguvu, na warudi, kila mtu kutoka njia yake mbaya na kutoka udhalimu ulio viganjani mwao.
sw.B: Watu na wanyama wote wafunikwe nguo za magunia. Wamlilie Mungu kwa nguvu zao zote, na kila mmoja aiache njia yake mbaya na udhalimu anaoutenda.
sw.R: Kila mtu, na hata wanyama, wavae nguo za magunia. Kila mtu amwombe Mungu kwa nguvu zake zote. Wote waache kutenda maovu, na waache kuwadhulumu wengine.

ko.L: 그리고 사람과 짐승은 굵은 베옷을 덮어쓰고, 힘껏 하나님께 부르짖어라. 그리고 각자 자기의 악한 길과 자기 손바닥에 있는 폭력에서 돌아서라.
ko.B: 사람과 짐승은 모두 굵은 베옷을 걸치고, 힘을 다해 하나님께 부르짖어라. 그리고 저마다 자기의 악한 길에서, 자기 손으로 저지르는 폭력에서 돌아서라.
ko.R: 사람이든 짐승이든 모두 베옷을 입어라. 모두 힘을 다해 하나님께 기도하여라. 모두 나쁜 짓을 그만두고, 다른 사람을 괴롭히는 일을 그쳐라.

decisions.choice: the violence that is in their palms: the wrong they do with their own hands
decisions.reason: Violence "in the hands" is wrong a person does and holds on to, whether cruelty or what was gained by it (Job 16:17; Isaiah 59:6). The king names the city's sin plainly. Assyria was known for the violence of its conquests (Nahum 3:1).

decisions.choice: turn from his evil way: repent, change one's whole way of life
decisions.reason: To "turn" is the Bible's word for repentance. "Evil" is the word used of Nineveh in 1:2. The king asks for more than fasting; he asks for a change of life (Jeremiah 18:11; 25:5).

decisions.choice: with strength (L); with all their might (B); with all their strength (R); the violence they do (B); stop hurting others (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what calling "with strength" means. They also turn "the violence in their palms" into the violence people do (m1). "Each" means every person in the city, so "his" takes a gender setting at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "they".

decisions.choice: "que se vuelvan cada uno de su mal camino" (L, B), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "cada uno ... su" already includes men and women, so the English span on "their|his" has no Spanish counterpart.

decisions.choice: "chacun ... sa voie" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Where the English needs {{gender:their|his}} for the pronoun, French "chacun" and "sa" are already inclusive, as the style guide says; no span is added.

decisions.choice: "revenir" for shuv (L, B), as the term sheet keeps it at every level in the prophets; Readable "arrête de faire le mal"
decisions.reason: The verb returns in 3:9-10 for God, and French keeps one verb so the reader hears the people turn and God turn.

decisions.choice: "자기 손바닥에 있는 폭력" (L); "자기 손으로 저지르는 폭력" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew image of violence "in their palms" (meaning decision); Balanced says it is what their hands do.

decisions.choice: "sự bạo ngược trong lòng bàn tay của họ"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "palms", which the meaning decision explains as the wrong done with their own hands; Balanced and Readable say it plainly.

source.text: מִֽי־יוֹדֵ֣עַ יָשׁ֔וּב וְנִחַ֖ם הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְשָׁ֛ב מֵחֲר֥וֹן אַפּ֖וֹ וְלֹ֥א נֹאבֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: Who knows? He may turn and relent, the God, and turn from [the] burning of his anger, and we will not perish.

en.L: Who knows? God may turn and relent, and turn from the burning of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger, and we will not perish."
en.B: Who knows? God may yet turn and change {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may turn back from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fierce anger, and we will not perish."
en.R: Who knows? God may change {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind and stop being angry with us. Then we will not die."

es.L: ¿Quién sabe? Puede que Dios se vuelva y se retracte, y se aparte del ardor de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira, y no pereceremos».
es.B: ¿Quién sabe? Tal vez Dios todavía se vuelva y desista; tal vez se aparte del ardor de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira, y no pereceremos».
es.R: ¿Quién sabe? Tal vez Dios cambie de parecer y deje de estar enojado con nosotros. Así no moriremos».

fr.L: Qui sait ? Dieu peut revenir et renoncer [à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} projet], et revenir de l’ardeur de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère, et nous ne périrons pas. »
fr.B: Qui sait ? Dieu peut encore revenir en arrière et renoncer à nous punir ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} peut revenir de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère ardente, et nous ne périrons pas. »
fr.R: Qui sait ? Dieu va peut-être renoncer à nous punir et ne plus être en colère contre nous. Alors nous ne mourrons pas. »

vi.L: Ai biết được? Đức Chúa Trời có thể quay lại và đổi ý, và quay khỏi cơn giận phừng phừng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và chúng ta sẽ không chết mất."
vi.B: Ai biết được? Có lẽ Đức Chúa Trời sẽ quay lại và đổi ý; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có thể nguôi cơn giận dữ dội, và chúng ta sẽ không chết mất."
vi.R: Ai biết được? Có thể Đức Chúa Trời sẽ đổi ý và thôi giận chúng ta. Khi ấy chúng ta sẽ không phải chết."

sw.L: Nani ajuaye? Huenda Mungu atageuka na kughairi, na kurudi kutoka ukali wa hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, nasi hatutaangamia."
sw.B: Nani anajua? Huenda Mungu bado atageuka na kughairi; huenda ataiacha hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kali, nasi hatutaangamia."
sw.R: Nani anajua? Huenda Mungu atabadili nia {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na kuacha kutukasirikia. Ndipo hatutakufa."

ko.L: 누가 알겠느냐? 하나님께서 돌이키시고 뜻을 돌이키셔서, 그분의 타오르는 진노에서 돌아서시면, 우리가 망하지 않을 것이다."
ko.B: 누가 알겠느냐? 하나님께서 돌아서서 뜻을 돌이키시고, 그 맹렬한 진노를 거두실지. 그러면 우리가 망하지 않을 것이다."
ko.R: 누가 알겠느냐? 하나님께서 마음을 바꾸셔서 더 이상 우리에게 화를 내지 않으실지도 모른다. 그러면 우리가 죽지 않을 것이다."

decisions.choice: relent: change his mind, turn from a course he has announced
decisions.reason: The verb is used of God turning from a punishment he has threatened when people turn from their sin (Exodus 32:12, 14; Jeremiah 18:8; Joel 2:13-14). It does not mean that God has made a mistake; it means that he responds to people. The same verb is used in verse 10 and in Jonah's complaint (4:2).

decisions.choice: Who knows? God may turn and relent: the same hope as Joel 2:14
decisions.reason: Joel 2:14 says "Who knows? He may turn and relent", and Moses prays "Turn from your burning anger, and relent" (Exodus 32:12). The king of Nineveh, who does not know Israel's God, hopes in the same words. He claims nothing; he can only hope.

decisions.choice: and we will not perish: the captain's words in 1:6
decisions.reason: The ship's captain said "Perhaps the god will give a thought to us, and we will not perish". The pagan king and the pagan captain hope for the same mercy.

decisions.choice: relent (L); change his mind (B, R); the burning of his anger (L); fierce anger (B); perish (L, B); die (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "change his mind" for "relent". Literal and Balanced keep "perish", as in 1:6 (m3). The double quotation mark closes the king's decree.

decisions.choice: "se retracte" (L); "desista" (B); "cambie de parecer" (R)
decisions.reason: The same Spanish words as Joel 2:13-14, where the same hope is voiced; "retractarse" is the settled Literal word for God relenting.

decisions.choice: "kughairi" (L, B); "kubadili nia" (R)
decisions.reason: God relenting is "kughairi" at Literal and Balanced and "kubadili nia yake" at Readable, as in the published Jeremiah (18:8; 26:3, 13, 19) and Exodus 32:14. The same words are used in 3:10 and 4:2.

decisions.choice: "nasi hatutaangamia"
decisions.reason: The same words as the captain's in 1:6, which the king's hope repeats.

decisions.choice: "누가 알겠느냐? … 돌이키시고 뜻을 돌이키셔서" (L); "돌아서서 뜻을 돌이키시고" (B); "마음을 바꾸셔서" (R), as the Korean Joel 2:14
decisions.reason: The same hope as Joel 2:14 (meaning decision), worded as the Korean Joel. "뜻을 돌이키다" / "마음을 바꾸다" for God relenting are the Jeremiah 18:8 words; "후회하다" would suggest regret over a mistake. The king speaks of God with -시- though he is a foreigner, as human speech about God does throughout.

decisions.choice: "우리가 망하지 않을 것이다" (L, B), as the captain's "우리가 망하지 않을지도" in 1:6
decisions.reason: The king's words repeat the captain's (meaning decision), so Literal and Balanced keep the same verb "망하다".

decisions.choice: "đổi ý" for God relenting, at every level
decisions.reason: As the published Jeremiah 18:8 and 26:3; "ăn năn" would suggest God had done wrong, which the meaning decision does not say. "chết mất" echoes the captain's words in 1:6, as the meaning decision notes.

decisions.choice: "renoncer" for God relenting at every level, never "se repentir"
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for the prophets: God changes the course he has announced; "se repentir" would suggest he had done wrong.

source.text: וַיַּ֤רְא הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶֽת־מַ֣עֲשֵׂיהֶ֔ם כִּי־שָׁ֖בוּ מִדַּרְכָּ֣ם הָרָעָ֑ה וַיִּנָּ֣חֶם הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים עַל־הָרָעָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר לַעֲשׂוֹת־לָהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א עָשָֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw the God their deeds, that they turned from their evil way; and relented the God concerning the evil which he had said to do to them, and he did not do [it].

en.L: And God saw their deeds, that they had turned from their evil way; and God relented concerning the evil that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would do to them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not do [it].
en.B: When God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil ways, God relented of the disaster {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would bring on them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not do it.
en.R: God saw what they did. He saw that they had stopped doing evil. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} changed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind and did not bring on them the disaster {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would bring.

es.L: Y vio Dios sus obras, que se habían vuelto de su mal camino; y se retractó Dios del mal que había dicho que les haría, y no [lo] hizo.
es.B: Cuando Dios vio lo que hacían, cómo se volvían de sus malos caminos, desistió del desastre que había dicho que traería sobre ellos, y no lo hizo.
es.R: Dios vio lo que hicieron. Vio que habían dejado de hacer el mal. Así que cambió de parecer y no les envió el desastre que había dicho que les enviaría.

fr.L: Et Dieu vit leurs œuvres, qu’ils étaient revenus de leur voie mauvaise ; et Dieu renonça au mal qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait dit qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur ferait, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne [le] fit pas.
fr.B: Quand Dieu vit ce qu’ils faisaient, comment ils revenaient de leur mauvaise conduite, Dieu renonça au malheur qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait dit qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ferait venir sur eux, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne le fit pas.
fr.R: Dieu a vu ce qu’ils faisaient. Il a vu qu’ils avaient arrêté de faire le mal. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a renoncé au malheur qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait dit qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} enverrait sur eux. Il ne l’a pas envoyé.

vi.L: Đức Chúa Trời thấy việc làm của họ, rằng họ đã quay lại khỏi đường ác của mình; và Đức Chúa Trời đổi ý về điều ác {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán là sẽ làm cho họ, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không làm [điều đó].
vi.B: Khi Đức Chúa Trời thấy việc họ làm, thấy họ đã từ bỏ đường lối gian ác của mình, thì Đức Chúa Trời đổi ý về tai họa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán sẽ giáng trên họ, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không giáng tai họa ấy nữa.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời thấy việc họ làm. Ngài thấy họ đã thôi làm điều ác. Vì vậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đổi ý và không giáng trên họ tai họa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán là sẽ giáng.

sw.L: Mungu akaona matendo yao, kwamba walikuwa wamerudi kutoka njia yao mbaya; naye Mungu akaghairi kuhusu ubaya aliosema kwamba atawatendea, wala hakuutenda.
sw.B: Mungu alipoona waliyoyafanya, jinsi walivyoiacha njia yao mbaya, Mungu aliyaghairi maafa aliyokuwa amesema atawaletea, wala hakuyaleta.
sw.R: Mungu aliona waliyoyafanya. Aliona kwamba wameacha kutenda maovu. Kwa hiyo alibadili nia {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, wala hakuwaletea maafa aliyokuwa amesema atawaletea.

ko.L: 그리고 하나님께서 그들의 행위, 곧 그들이 그들의 악한 길에서 돌아선 것을 보셨다. 그리고 하나님께서 그들에게 하겠다고 말씀하신 재앙에 대하여 뜻을 돌이키시고, [그것을] 행하지 않으셨다.
ko.B: 하나님께서는 그들이 한 일, 곧 그들이 악한 길에서 돌아선 것을 보셨다. 그래서 하나님께서는 그들에게 내리겠다고 말씀하신 재앙에 대해 뜻을 돌이키시고, 그 재앙을 내리지 않으셨다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 그들이 한 일을 보셨다. 그들이 악한 일을 그만둔 것을 보셨다. 그래서 하나님께서는 마음을 바꾸셨다. 그들에게 내리겠다고 하신 재앙을 내리지 않으셨다.

decisions.choice: their evil way ... the evil he had said he would do: one word for their wickedness and for the disaster
decisions.reason: The same word, used throughout the book (see 1:2), names the evil the people did and the evil, that is the disaster, God threatened. When they turned from the one, God turned from the other, as Jeremiah 18:7-8 describes.

decisions.choice: God relented: the threatened judgment was not carried out
decisions.reason: Jonah's message gave no condition, but the story shows that God's warnings call people to turn (Jeremiah 18:7-10). Elsewhere Scripture says that God does not change his mind as a human does (Numbers 23:19; 1 Samuel 15:29). Both speak of the same God: his purpose stands, and he answers those who turn to him. This is what Jonah complains of in 4:2.

decisions.choice: God saw their deeds: he responded to what they did, not only to their fast
decisions.reason: It was their turning from evil, the change in their lives that the king called for (verse 8), that God saw.

decisions.choice: evil ... evil (L); evil ways ... disaster (B); evil ... disaster (R); relented (L, B); changed his mind (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "evil" twice so the reader can see the one word (m1). Balanced and Readable say "disaster" for what God threatened. Readable says "changed his mind", as in verse 9.

decisions.choice: "mal camino ... mal" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps one Spanish word for the Hebrew word that names both their wickedness and the disaster; Balanced and Readable use "desastre" for the second.

decisions.choice: "voie mauvaise ... le mal" (L), "mauvaise conduite ... le malheur" (B, R)
alternatives: "le mal" for both at every level
decisions.reason: Literal keeps one word for their evil and the evil God had threatened, as the English meaning decision notes; Balanced and Readable separate the senses.

decisions.choice: "악한 길" for their evil; "재앙" for the evil God had said he would do
decisions.reason: One Hebrew word serves for both (meaning decision); Korean has no single word for wickedness and disaster, so even Literal says "재앙" for what God threatened, as Jeremiah 18:8 L, and God is not heard planning wickedness.

decisions.choice: "đường ác" ... "điều ác" (L); "đường lối gian ác" ... "tai họa" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: one word for their wickedness and the disaster; Literal keeps "ác" in both places so the play can be seen, as the English Literal does.
